items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: You see, as I told you, I signed up with Vincent Lopez's office.

ctx.x: What years would you say that they started with a real distinctive big band style? Would it be about like the late twenties, or somewhere in there?

I would say the middle twenties. Middle twenties? Yes, yes. Duke Ellington and such, you know, and Ray Miller. You see, as I told you, I signed up with Vincent Lopez's office. Not that I needed a job, because I was working. But it's good to have somebody looking out for your interest, you know.

items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1969-12-04
items.q: So I signed up with Vincent Lopez. And he appointed Mrs. Marvin Fuller, Mrs. Earl Fuller as my manager.

ctx.x: But your New York recordings had a two-bone. They're too long you say? No, there's a tuba, tuba player.

I had a tuba player, Barney Aquilino. He was with James Barney. I got him afterwards in New York. And he was more or less my promoter. He got me in the middle of a dance hall. I wore up in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania. There was two dance halls, big ball, beautiful big ball. They were fighting each other. And I happened to play at the six day bicycle races. You see I lived a long life, and I'll tell you a long, I mean a musical life. I'm playing at the six day bicycle races for the benefit of poor children. And in…
She was in early movies, in silent movies?
